draft.briefing: Hey, you're at the Gateway of India! This 26-metre basalt arch was put up to mark King George V's landing in 1911, and in 1948 it was the spot from where the last British troops left India.
draft.hungryLine: Bademiya, which started in 1946 as a makeshift seekh kabab counter, is a Colaba food landmark worth hunting down.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The Taj Mahal Palace Hotel is right opposite, the National Gallery of Modern Art is about 9 minutes on foot, and the Art Deco Dhanraj Mahal is close by too.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Try the Mumbai Port Trust Garden, off a side street of Colaba Causeway, for views of the port, the naval yards and the sunset.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The Maharashtra Police Headquarters nearby started life as the Royal Alfred Sailors' Home for sick European sailors, and later housed the state legislature until 1982.

spots.name: Taj Mahal Palace Hotel
spots.detail: Right opposite · The 1903 Indo-Saracenic landmark facing the Gateway

spots.name: National Gallery of Modern Art
spots.detail: 9 min walk · Exhibitions inside the old Cowasji Jehangir Hall

spots.name: Dhanraj Mahal
spots.detail: Near the Gateway · A 1930s Art Deco palace in pale pink sandstone

tips.title: Stroll Churchgate to Colaba.
tips.body: The wide, clean pavements from Churchgate down to Colaba are the best way to see the old city centre, ideally in the cooler hours.

tips.title: Skip the Yacht Club plans.
tips.body: The Royal Bombay Yacht Club next door is for members only, so admire it from outside.

story.title: The Taj opens
story.body: The Taj Mahal Hotel opened on the waterfront in the Indo-Saracenic style, and was long counted among the finest hotels in the East.

story.title: A king lands
story.body: King George V landed here for his coronation as Emperor of India, the first British monarch to visit India.

story.title: Building the arch
story.body: The foundation stone went in in 1913, George Wittet's design was approved in 1914, and the basalt arch was finished in 1924.

story.title: The last troops leave
story.body: A year after independence, the last British troops left India through the Gateway.
The Taj Mahal Palace Hotel was one of the main targets of the 2008 Mumbai attacks, along with nearby Leopold Cafe.
